rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.e1: Before we start, a reminder from the earlier lessons: with one square between them on the same file, the kings are in direct opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.e2: Whoever has just moved has the opposition: the other king must move and give way.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.e3: Here it is White to move. If the white king moves, Black keeps the opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.e4: But White also has the pawn on b5, far from the kings.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! The pawn advances, the kings stay where they were, and the move passes to Black.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to advance the pawn: the kings stay where they were, and the move passes to Black.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5c5.1: The king moved: now it is Black who can take the opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5c5.2: The black king goes to c7, facing the white king with one square between them: Black has the opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5e5.1: The king moves away from the b5-pawn, and the black king is free to come closer to it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5e5.2: The black king goes to c7, next to b6. If the pawn advances, the black king captures it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5d4.1: The king steps back, and Black can advance the king and take the opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5d4.2: The black king advances to d6. The kings face each other again, and Black holds the opposition, having just moved.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5c4.1: The king steps back, and the black king gains room to get close to the pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5c4.2: The black king advances to d6, one step from c6. If the pawn advances, the black king catches it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5e4.1: The king steps back to e4 and leaves the b5-pawn far from any support.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.err.d5e4.2: The white king moved away from the pawn. The black king goes to d6 and reaches the pawn first.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing as White and see how Black defends.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king was stalemated: stalemate is a draw.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: With the opposition, the black king always blocks the way.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: With the opposition, the black king always blocks the way.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: the kings have not moved, but now it is Black who must play.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l2: The opposition went to White without the white king moving. The pawn move simply passed the turn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l3: In the earlier lessons, the side that took the opposition with its move had the tempo. Here, the pawn move did that for White.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l4: Without the opposition, the black king must give way and steps back to d8.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l5: The white king advances to d6 and faces it again: direct opposition.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king goes to c8, next to b8, the promotion square.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l7: The white king follows to c6. Once again, Black must give way.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l8: Forced to give way, the black king steps aside to d8.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l9: Now the pawn advances, protected by the king, and the black king can no longer reach b8.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l11: Let's go back to the starting position. With the king, White would give up the opposition; with the pawn, the move passed to Black.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex1.l12: Remember: a pawn move, without moving the kings, also passes the turn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's look at another example. Each king protects a pawn: White's protects f4; Black's protects f5.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.e2: The f-pawns are blocked. Whoever has to move the king abandons their pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.e3: In the earlier lessons we saw the name for this: zugzwang. Here it applies to both sides.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h4.1: The king moves before the black king. Whoever moves the king first abandons the pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h4.2: On h4, the white king no longer protects the f4 pawn, and the black king captures it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h5.1: With the king, White spends the turn; the a-pawn is the one that should have passed it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h5.2: The white king steps to h5. The f4 pawn is left alone, and the black king captures it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h6.1: The king retreats for no reason: the a-pawn would pass the turn without abandoning anything.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5h6.2: The white king retreats to h6, far from the pawns, and the black king captures the f4 pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5g6.1: The king trades the defence of f4 for an attack on f5.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5g6.2: On g6, the white king threatens the f5 pawn, but it is protected. It is the f4 pawn that falls.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5f6.1: The king steps up to attack f5 head-on and stops defending f4.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.err.g5f6.2: On f6, the white king cannot capture on f5, which is protected. The black king captures on f4.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.p: White to play. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! The a-pawn passes the turn, and now Black has to move the king.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to advance the a-pawn: it passes the turn, and Black must move the king.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not one we are studying here. Let's go back to the position.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.volta: Let's go back to the position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l1: The f5 pawn cannot advance, and the black king has to leave e4.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l2: The black king goes to d4 and stops protecting the f5 pawn.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l3: The white king captures the f5 pawn. Now the f4 pawn is free, with its king nearby.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l4: Let's go back to the position. The a-pawn was far from the fight, but it decided it.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l5: A pawn move kept only to pass the turn at the right moment is called a reserve tempo.
rot.reserve.ideia.ex2.l6: Whoever has one more reserve tempo wins the zugzwang fight.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.1: First position: the Capablanca structure from the earlier lessons, with blocked pawns on b and h.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.2: Now White has an extra pawn, on a2. Watch how it will be used.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.3: The white king steps up to e2, on its way to the centre.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.4: The black king comes to e6 and also heads for the centre.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.5: The white king reaches e3. In the centre, the kings will fight for the opposition.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.6: The black king faces it from e5: Black has the opposition.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.7: Without the a-pawn, White would have to move the king and give way.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.8: But White has a reserve tempo: the a-pawn advances one square, and the move passes to Black.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.9: Now the black king must give way. It goes to d5.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.10: The white king goes through f4, on its way to the h5 pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.11: The black king runs to the queenside pawns, and the white king reaches g5.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.12: The white king captures the h5 pawn. The h-pawn is free and promotes before the black pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.13: Let's go back to the starting position. Other moves also win; what you must not do is lose the a-pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.14: And what if White pushed the a-pawn two squares?
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.15: The black b5-pawn captures it: the a-pawn is gone, and with it the reserve tempo. Now White no longer wins.
rot.reserve.demos.capablanca.16: Push the a-pawn just one square: that way it is not captured, and that push is your reserve tempo.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.1: Now thinking from Black's side, and the board has turned. It is the position from the second example, without White's a-pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.2: White to play, and White has no pawn move to pass the turn.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.3: The white king has to move. It goes to h5 and stops protecting the f4 pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.4: The black king captures the f4 pawn.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.5: The white king comes back, and the black king goes to e4, beside the pawn's path, to let it advance.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.6: With the king alongside, the pawn advances and will promote.
rot.reserve.demos.semReserva.7: The same position changes hands with one reserve tempo more or less.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.fim: The pawn passed the turn, and the white king kept the opposition to the end.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6g5.1: The king goes to g5 before the pawn spends its reserve move, and the black king chooses its square.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6g5.2: The black king goes to e7 and on to f8, in front of the pawn’s path: your king does not get through, and it is a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6g7.1: The king goes to g7 and leaves the h3 pawn far from its support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6g7.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, reaches g4: it captures the pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h5.1: The king goes to h5, in front of the pawn, but on the edge file it blocks the path itself.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h5.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to f6: your king is stuck on the h-file, and it is a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h6.1: The king goes to h6 and climbs without the pawn: the black king comes close to it.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h6.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to f6: your king is stuck on the h-file, and it is a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h7.1: The king goes to h7 and abandons the h3 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.err.g6h7.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, reaches g4 to capture it.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h4h5.1: The pawn advances too early: the black king reaches f8, in front of its path.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.h4h5.2: The black king goes to f8. Your king does not control the squares in front of the pawn, and the black king stands before it: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6f5.1: The king retreats to f5 and gives the black king back the f7 square and the path to the corner.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6f5.2: The black king goes to f7, facing your king, and on to g7: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6g5.1: The king retreats to g5 and lets the black king reach f7.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6g5.2: The black king goes to f7 and, when your king climbs to h6, takes f6: the pawn does not get through.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h5.1: The king goes to h5, in front of the pawn, and leaves f6 to the black king.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h5.2: The black king goes to f6. Your king, on the h-file, cannot get out from in front of the pawn: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h6.1: The king goes to h6, and the black king gains f6, beside it.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h6.2: The black king goes to f6 and, after the pawn advances, to f7: your king does not leave the h-file.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h7.1: The king goes to h7 and leaves f6 and f7 to the black king.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v2.err.g6h7.2: The black king goes to f6 and, after the pawn advances, to f7: your king does not leave the corner.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h6.1: The king goes back to h6, in front of the pawn, and lets the black king come closer.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h6.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to f6: your king is stuck on the h-file.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h7.1: The king goes to h7, in front of the pawn, and lets the black king come closer.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h7.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to f6: your king does not leave the h-file.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7f8.1: The king goes to f8 and moves away from the pawn, which is left without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7f8.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to g5: it captures the pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7g8.1: The king goes to g8 and moves away from the pawn, which is left without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7g8.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to g5: it captures the pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h8.1: The king goes into the corner and leaves the pawn without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v3.err.g7h8.2: The black king goes to f5 and, after the pawn advances, to g5: it captures the pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h6.1: The king goes to h6, in front of the pawn, and the black king gains f6.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h6.2: The black king goes to f6. Your king has to go back to h7, and the black king follows it to f7: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7f7.1: The king goes to f7 and abandons the h5 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7f7.2: The black king goes to g5 and captures the h5 pawn on the next move.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h7.1: The king goes to h7, in front of the pawn, and the black king gains f6.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h7.2: The black king goes to f6 and, after the pawn advances, to f7: your king does not leave the corner.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7f8.1: The king goes to f8 and moves away from the h5 pawn, which is left without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7f8.2: The black king goes to g5 and captures the pawn when it advances.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7g8.1: The king goes to g8 and moves away from the h5 pawn, which is left without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7g8.2: The black king goes to g5 and captures the pawn when it advances.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h8.1: The king goes into the corner and leaves the h5 pawn without support.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v4.err.g7h8.2: The black king goes to g5 and captures the pawn when it advances.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7f7.1: The king goes to f7 and abandons the h6 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7f7.2: The black king captures the h6 pawn, and only the kings remain: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7f8.1: The king goes to f8 and abandons the h6 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7f8.2: The black king captures the h6 pawn, and only the kings remain: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7g8.1: The king goes to g8 and abandons the h6 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7g8.2: The black king captures the h6 pawn, and only the kings remain: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7h8.1: The king goes into the corner and abandons the h6 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.ataque.v5.err.g7h8.2: The black king captures the h6 pawn, and only the kings remain: a draw.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a3.1: The king goes to a3 and moves away from the c5 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a3.2: The white king captures the c5 pawn, and the c4 pawn is free: the win slips away.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4b3.1: The king goes to b3 and attacks the c4 pawn, but the white king protects it.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4b3.2: The white king captures on c5 and protects the c4 pawn at the same time: the win slips away.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4c3.1: The king goes to c3 and also attacks the c4 pawn, which stays protected.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4c3.2: Without protection, the c5 pawn falls, and the white c4 pawn is free to advance.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a4.1: The king retreats to a4 and no longer touches the c5 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a4.2: The white king steps into c5. Black is left with only the h-pawn, and the draw is certain.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a5.1: The king goes to a5, but from there it does not protect the c5 pawn.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.err.b4a5.2: The white king captures on c5 and protects the c4-pawn: the win slips away.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.reserve.pratica.defesa.fim: The h-pawn passed the turn, and now the white king must abandon the c4 pawn.
